representation_evidence.observation: The board presents a compact incident-response workflow divided into “1 · Detect & triage,” “2 · Coordinate & mitigate,” and “3 · Resolve & learn.”

representation_evidence.locator: objects sections intake, response, and learning
representation_evidence.observation: Three ordered process sections organize the complete incident lifecycle without adding unrelated operational machinery.

verdict.strongest_covered_cluster: The declared-incident response loop is especially complete: shared record creation, service-owner assignment, parallel on-call coordination and owner mitigation, same-signal verification, resolution gating, and failed-verification return to the owner are all represented.
verdict.most_consequential_gap: The intake boundary is not fully explicit: the board shows a high-confidence alert entering duplicate grouping, but does not visibly identify Monitoring as the source or the Alert Manager as the receiving component.
verdict.coverage_summary: The board covers the full alert-to-learning lifecycle and all major failure, retry, escalation, resolution, and follow-up paths. Two qualifiers are only partial: the monitoring-to-alert-manager boundary is implicit, and the active status-maintenance node does not explicitly identify the status as the public status page. Weighted coverage is 32.5 of 34.
